ct_mansfield_grove_boulder.blurb: Mansfield Grove Boulder is a lone glacial erratic in East Haven, Connecticut, tucked behind a school and close to the Greenway trail. It stands roughly nine feet tall, so this is a low-ball, pad-and-spotter style stop rather than a full day out. Thirteen problems cover a wide spread: several easy ones around V0 to V1, a middle group in the V3 to V5 range, and a couple of much harder lines at the top end. Expect crimpy, powerful pulling on a blocky, rugged face. It suits a quick after-work session or a warm-up near town.

ga_riverside_cliffs_area.blurb: Riverside Cliffs Area is a collection of small cliffs and boulders beside the Chattahoochee River in the Palisades, on the north side of metro Atlanta. Thirteen climbs mix short trad lines and top-rope routes, mostly from 5.6 to 5.9, with a handful of boulder problems from the easiest grades up to about V4. Most cliffs can be reached from above and have trees for building anchors, and the trail along the base can be rough, so some parties find it simpler to rappel in. It is a modest, low-key spot for beginners and easy mileage.

ri_goat_rock.blurb: Goat Rock is a prominent cliff in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island, close to picnic area 9C and easy to spot as you approach. It is the park's one real top-rope face, with seven top-rope lines from easy 5.6 climbing through 5.9 and a couple of hard 5.11 test pieces. Rigging usually calls for trad gear, or very long slings or a static line. A small boulder section alongside adds six problems, mostly in the easier grades with one far harder outlier. Good for a mixed day with a beginner group.

ri_egg_the.blurb: The Egg is a single boulder sitting on a small hill in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island. It looks unassuming until you start pulling on it, and the problems here are strong and high quality. Thirteen boulder problems run from V2 all the way up to V12, with a good share of difficult lines in the V8 to V12 range and just a few easier ones to get started on. In summer the foliage hides it from the road, so it is easy to walk past. A destination mainly for stronger boulderers.

ri_lower_heart.blurb: Lower Heart is a boulder in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island, on the far side of the swamp from the larger Heart boulder. The left half offers slab problems, while the right half leans back slightly and climbs more steeply. Thirteen problems range from V0 up to V6, with a cluster around V3 and a few hard lines on the steeper side, so it has something for beginners and for those pushing harder. It can be reached by trail from the Heart or from the Warmup area.

ri_the_fissure_boulder.blurb: The Fissure Boulder is a short wall right beside one of the main roads through Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island, directly opposite the entrance to Lodi's Warmup. It makes a handy quick stop on the way to the Sit Down or Pond Cave areas. Thirteen boulder problems run from V0 to V5, mostly in the V1 to V3 range, with a single V5 sit start at the top end. A friendly spot for warming up, easy mileage and moderate problems rather than for hard projects.

ri_coke_bottle_boulder.blurb: Coke Bottle Boulder is a tall boulder in Lincoln Woods, Rhode Island, with some committing highball problems. A few lines start from a ledge on the upper portion, while the rest climb the taller, lower side. Of its thirteen climbs, twelve are boulder problems, from V1 up to V8, with most falling in the V1 to V5 range, plus one hard sport line. Bring plenty of pads and a spotter. It is best for confident climbers comfortable with height, though a few easier problems give a gentler start.
